key_insight: STAR-XPC predicts X-ray transmission through polymer composites in milliseconds, closely matching computationally expensive Monte Carlo reference simulations.
engineering_relevance: The model could accelerate screening of polyethylene-based radiation shields across composition, thickness, and X-ray tube voltage.
method: Encode molecular constituents with pretrained ChemBERTa embeddings and include their mass fractions.
Use a permutation-invariant Set Transformer for mixtures of up to 11 constituents plus four bulk physical descriptors.
Train on transmission ratios generated by an automated PENELOPE/penEasy simulation pipeline.
evidence_signal: On 4,697 simulated configurations, leakage-free, jointly stratified 10-fold cross-validation achieved R² = 0.9988 and median absolute percentage error = 1.15%.
watch_item: Performance outside the studied polyethylene-based composites, 0.15–2.5 mm thicknesses, and four tube voltages—and agreement with physical experiments—remains unestablished.
paper_title: STAR-XPC: Set Transformer for Estimating X-ray Transmission in Polymer Composites
